Making Japanese curry? 🍛  Don’t just chop everything into random sizes. The way you cut your vegetables actually matters, especially if you want them nicely cooked and not disappear in curry. 🥕 𝐂𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐨𝐭 → rangiri cut Cutting it into irregular rolling pieces gives you different surfaces while keeping the pieces relatively similar in size, so they cook evenly. 🥔 𝐏𝐨𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐨 → bite-size chunks Not too small, so they have enough structure to hold their shape while becoming tender. 🧅 𝐎𝐧𝐢𝐨𝐧 → wedges Keeping the onion in wedges allows it to soften and become sweet without completely disappearing into the curry. It’s a small step, but proper cutting makes a difference in cooking time, texture and how your curry comes together. Save this for the next time you make Japanese kare raisu 🍛🇯🇵 𝘑𝘢𝘱𝘢𝘯𝘦𝘴𝘦 𝘤𝘰𝘰𝘬𝘪𝘯𝘨, 𝘮𝘢𝘥𝘦 𝘦𝘢𝘴𝘪𝘦𝘳 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘛𝘩𝘦𝘳𝘮𝘰𝘮𝘪𝘹. 𝘐𝘧 𝘺𝘰𝘶’𝘳𝘦 𝘤𝘶𝘳𝘪𝘰𝘶𝘴 𝘢𝘣𝘰𝘶𝘵 𝘰𝘸𝘯𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘰𝘯𝘦, 𝘮𝘦𝘴𝘴𝘢𝘨𝘦 𝘮𝘦.
